sections.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Define the Bernoulli trial as the foundation: an experiment with exactly two outcomes (Success/Failure) and a constant probability 'p'.
sections.example: Visualizing a coin flip: Heads (Success, p=0.5) vs. Tails (Failure, q=0.5).

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution
sections.content: Explain that a Binomial Distribution counts the number of successes in 'n' independent Bernoulli trials. Introduce the mnemonic BINS: Binary, Independent, Number (fixed), Success (constant probability).
sections.example: A robot dog attempting 5 jumps; each jump is either a 'Success' (lands perfectly) or 'Failure' (stumbles).

sections.title: The Probability Mass Function (PMF)
sections.content: Introduce the formula P(X=k) = C(n, k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Use a graphical bar chart animation to show how 'n' and 'p' shape the distribution histogram.
sections.example: Calculating the probability of the robot dog landing exactly 3 out of 5 jumps.

sections.title: Mean and Variance: The Intuition
sections.content: Explain the expected value (mean = np) and variance (npq) as the 'center of mass' and 'spread' of the histogram, visually showing how changing 'p' shifts the distribution.
sections.example: If the robot dog has a 60% success rate, on average, how many successful jumps should we expect in 100 trials?

sections.title: Application and Wrap-up
sections.content: Summarize how binomial distributions model real-world scenarios involving binary outcomes. Briefly touch upon how it relates to normal distribution approximations as n increases.
sections.example: Predicting success rates in quality control for a smartphone assembly line using binomial modeling.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
lecture_lines: A Bernoulli trial has two outcomes: success or failure.
It relies on a constant probability, p.
animations: Show a coin flipping, labeling Head (#FFD700) and Tail (#00BFFF).
Flash the Head result to emphasize a successful trial.
Color the trial outcome label to #FF4500 when success occurs.

storyboard.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution
lecture_lines: Binomial distributions count successes in n independent trials.
Remember BINS: Binary, Independent, Number, Success.
The number of trials n is fixed.
animations: Display n independent trials in a row.
Show k successes occurring among n trials.
Use color #32CD32 to highlight the chosen successes.

storyboard.title: The Probability Mass Function (PMF)
lecture_lines: The PMF calculates probability for exactly k successes.
Visual histograms show how n and p change shape.
animations: Show the binomial coefficient formula C(n, k).
Display the p^k term, coloring p as #FF6347.
Combine all terms into the final PMF formula.
Flash the complete formula to emphasize the PMF structure.

storyboard.title: Mean and Variance: The Intuition
lecture_lines: Variance equals n times p times q.
animations: Represent the mean as E[X] = np.
Use arrows to correlate parameters with the formula parts.
Flash the resulting value to illustrate expected outcome.

storyboard.title: Application and Wrap-up
lecture_lines: Binomial models solve real-world binary problems.
Quality control uses these models effectively.
animations: Display a real-world example scenario icon.
Summarize the binomial application steps on screen.
Fade in a 'Conclusion' text to end the section.
